explanation: When `ast.literal_eval` succeeds on a quoted string (e.g., `"hello"`), the code re-wraps the evaluated result with the original quote character, returning a string like `'hello'` (with literal quote characters) instead of the bare string `hello`, which changes the previously returned value and will break callers expecting an unquoted string.
